content_sections.heading: About CWC
content_sections.text: The Central Waqf Council (CWC), New Delhi, is a statutory body under the Ministry of Minority Affairs, Government of India. The Waqf Division of the Ministry, at Deendayal Antyodaya Bhawan, CGO Complex, Lodhi Road, New Delhi, issued this vacancy as Office Memorandum F. No. Waq-18/1/2025-Coord-MoMA dated 21 September 2026.

content_sections.heading: Where and How to Send
content_sections.text: Deputy Secretary (Waqf), Ministry of Minority Affairs, Room No. 1127 B-4 Wing, 11th Floor, Pt. Deendayal Antyodaya Bhawan, CGO Complex, Lodhi Road, New Delhi 110003. Fill in the Proforma "Application for the post of Secretary, Central Waqf Council (on foreign deputation basis (including short term contract))" and paste a passport-size photograph on it. Give your name, postal address, telephone, fax and e-mail, your present post with Pay Level (or Grade Pay), and the post you hold on a regular basis in your parent department. A retired officer gives the last designation and the post they retired from. Fill in the details of your past service: the post, the pay scale or Grade Pay or Pay Level, the period, and the nature of the duties performed. List your essential and desirable qualifications with the name and year of the degree, the university and the year of passing. Then sign the form and add your name, e-mail ID, the place and the date. Have the forwarding office fill in its part of the form: the office's name and category, the date of your continuous employment in the present grade, your present pay level and basic pay, and the certificate verifying your service particulars. The office also encloses your Cadre and Vigilance clearance. Put the application in a sealed envelope and write on it: "APPLICATION FOR THE POST OF SECRETARY, CENTRAL WAQF COUNCIL" . Send the envelope through proper channel to the address above so that it reaches within the 45-day limit.

content_sections.heading: Posts, Eligibility and Pay
content_sections.text: The post of Secretary, Central Waqf Council is filled by deputation (including short-term contract) from: Serving officers of the Central Government or the State Government or Union territory Administration or public sector undertaking or autonomous or statutory body who: hold analogous posts on a regular basis in the parent cadre or Department; or have five years' regular service in the grade, rendered after appointment to it on a regular basis, in a post at Level 12 in the Pay Matrix (Rs. 78800-209200) or equivalent; Or retired officers of the rank of Deputy Secretary or Director or above in the Central Government. Essential: A Bachelors' degree or equivalent from a recognised University or institute; and at least five years' experience of administrative, financial and legal matters. Desirable: experience in the field of waqf management. Serving officers: the maximum age limit for appointment on deputation is not exceeding fifty-six years as on the closing date for receipt of applications. Retired officers: the age should not be more than 62 years as on the last date for submission of the application. The official notification gives the full eligibility conditions for the post. Pay of the post: PB-4: Rs. 37400-67,000/- + GP Rs. 8700/- (Level 13 in the Pay Matrix as per the 7th Pay Commission). Serving officers: if a serving officer of the Central Government or the State Government or Union territory Administration or public sector undertaking or autonomous or statutory body is selected, their pay will be protected. The other allowances, such as Transportation allowance, HRA and Deputation Allowance, will be paid as applicable to Central Government employees on an equivalent scale of pay and Grade Pay. Retired officers: a retired person who draws a pension from any source gets a fixed monthly remuneration. It is worked out by deducting the basic pension from the pay drawn at the time of retirement. The remuneration stays the same for the term of the contract, with no annual increment or percentage increase during the contract period. Serving officers: the period of deputation, including any period of deputation in another ex-cadre post held immediately before this appointment in the same or another organisation or department, shall ordinarily not exceed four years. It is also subject to the age of superannuation set by the Government of India. Retired officers: the initial period of appointment is two years. With the approval of the competent authority, further extensions are allowed only up to a total tenure of four years or until the officer reaches the age of sixty-five, whichever is earlier. Terms and conditions of service that the Recruitment Rules of the CWC do not explicitly cover will be governed by the relevant provisions of the FR-SRs and by the deputation rules, regulations and instructions issued by the Central Government.

content_sections.heading: Enclosures
content_sections.text: The prescribed application form (Proforma), duly filled in and signed, in original, with a passport-size photograph pasted on it Forwarding letters from the employer (the application goes through proper channel) Integrity Certificate Vigilance Clearance (and Cadre clearance, enclosed by the forwarding office) Attested copies of the Annual Confidential Reports (ACRs) for the last five years; retired officials send the latest five years before retirement The forwarding office's part of the form, with its certificate that your service particulars have been verified against the service records

content_sections.heading: Important Instructions
content_sections.text: Forward an application only for an official who can be relieved immediately if selected. A candidate who has been selected will not be allowed to withdraw their candidature later. Submitting an application does not give a candidate any claim to selection, interview or appointment. The Ministry has the right to reject any application without giving a reason.

faq.question: Q1. How many vacancies are there in CWC Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: CWC Recruitment 2026 has 1 vacancy for the post of Secretary, Central Waqf Council, New Delhi. The notice does not print a number, so the one advertised post counts as 1 vacancy.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply for the CWC Secretary post?
faq.answer: The application must reach the Deputy Secretary (Waqf), Ministry of Minority Affairs, New Delhi, within 45 days from the date the advertisement is published in Employment News.

faq.question: Q3. What qualification is required for Secretary, Central Waqf Council?
faq.answer: The essential requirements are a Bachelors' degree or equivalent from a recognised University or institute and at least five years' experience of administrative, financial and legal matters. Experience in the field of waqf management is desirable.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit for the CWC Secretary post?
faq.answer: For serving officers on deputation, the age limit is not exceeding 56 years as on the closing date for receipt of applications. For retired officers, the age should not be more than 62 years as on the last date for submission of the application.

faq.question: Q5. What is the pay for Secretary, Central Waqf Council?
faq.answer: The post carries PB-4: Rs. 37400-67,000/- + GP Rs. 8700/- (Level 13 in the Pay Matrix as per the 7th Pay Commission). A selected serving officer's pay is protected, and Transportation allowance, HRA and Deputation Allowance are paid as applicable to Central Government employees on an equivalent scale.

faq.question: Q6. Can retired employees apply, and how is their pay fixed?
faq.answer: Yes. Retired officers of the rank of Deputy Secretary or Director or above in the Central Government can apply, up to 62 years of age. They get a fixed monthly remuneration equal to the pay drawn at retirement minus the basic pension, with no increment or percentage increase during the contract.

faq.question: Q7. How do I apply for CWC Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Send the prescribed application form, filled in and signed, in original through proper channel with forwarding letters, in a sealed envelope. The address is Deputy Secretary (Waqf), Ministry of Minority Affairs, Room No. 1127 B-4 Wing, 11th Floor, Pt. Deendayal Antyodaya Bhawan, CGO Complex, Lodhi Road, New Delhi 110003.

faq.question: Q8. What should be written on the envelope?
faq.answer: Write "APPLICATION FOR THE POST OF SECRETARY, CENTRAL WAQF COUNCIL" on the sealed envelope.

faq.question: Q9. Is the CWC Secretary post permanent, and how long is the tenure?
faq.answer: No. The post is filled on deputation basis (including short-term contract) on foreign service terms. Deputation ordinarily does not exceed four years. Retired officers are appointed for two years at first, with extensions allowed up to a total of four years or age 65, whichever is earlier.

faq.question: Q10. Which documents must go with the application?
faq.answer: The application must include an Integrity Certificate, Vigilance Clearance, and attested copies of the ACRs for the last five years. Retired officials send the ACRs for the latest five years before retirement.
